text:
Predicates:
Allowed(x) ::: Pets are allowed in managed building x.
DepositRequired(x) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in managed building x.
EqualOrMore(x) ::: The security deposit is either equal to or more than x.
IsPet(x) ::: x is a pet.
IsCat(x) ::: x is a cat.
IsBuilding(x) ::: x is a building.
MonthlyRent(x, y) ::: The monthly rent at building x is y dollars.
MoveInWith(x, y) ::: Person x moves in with pet y.
PriceLessThan(x, y) ::: The price of x is less than y.
RentApartment(x) ::: Person x will rent an apartment.
Premises:
∃x (IsBuilding(x) ∧ Allowed(x)) ::: Pets are allowed in some managed buildings.
∀x (DepositRequired(x) → ∃y (EqualOrMore(y) ∧ IsDollar(y))) ::: A deposit is required to rent an apartment in a managed building.
IsCat(fluffy) ∧ IsPet(fluffy) ∧ IsCat(tomCat) ∧ MoveInWith(tom, fluffy) ::: Fluffy is Tom's cat.
∀x (IsCat(x) → IsPet(x)) ::: Cats are pets.
IsBuilding(oliveGarden) ∧ Allowed(oliveGarden) ::: The Olive Garden is a managed building.
MonthlyRent(oliveGarden, 2000) ::: The monthly rent at the Olive Garden is $2000.
RentApartment(tom) ↔ (MoveInWith(tom, fluffy) ∧ PriceLessThan(1500, 2000)) ::: Tom will rent an apartment in a managed building if and only if he is allowed to move in with Fluffy, and the security deposit is no more than $1500.
PriceLessThan(2000, 1500) ::: 2000$ is more than $1500.
Conclusion:
EqualOrMore(2000) ::: The security deposit at the Olive Garden is either $2000 or more.
